question: A male newborn born at 27 weeks' gestation is evaluated for rapid breathing and hypoxia shortly after birth. His mother had no prenatal care. Cardiopulmonary examination shows normal heart sounds, intercostal retractions, and nasal flaring. An x-ray of the chest shows low lung volumes, air bronchograms, and diffuse ground-glass opacities. He is started on nasal continuous positive airway pressure. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

options.A: Bilateral pleural effusions on lung ultrasound
options.B: Corkscrew-shaped organisms on umbilical cord culture
options.C: Hyaline membranes lining the alveoli on lung biopsy

A. Bilateral pleural effusions on lung ultrasound
B. Corkscrew-shaped organisms on umbilical cord culture
C. Hyaline membranes lining the alveoli on lung biopsy

none.text:
The newborn is premature (27 weeks gestation), has respiratory distress (rapid breathing, hypoxia, intercostal retractions, nasal flaring), and chest x-ray findings consistent with respiratory distress syndrome (RDS). RDS is caused by a deficiency of surfactant in premature infants. Surfactant reduces surface tension in the alveoli, preventing them from collapsing.

A. Bilateral pleural effusions on lung ultrasound: Pleural effusions are not typical of RDS. They are more common in other conditions like pneumonia or congenital heart disease.

B. Corkscrew-shaped organisms on umbilical cord culture: Corkscrew-shaped organisms are associated with umbilical cord infection, such as *Chorioamnionitis*. This is not the primary concern in a newborn with RDS.

C. Hyaline membranes lining the alveoli on lung biopsy: Hyaline membranes are characteristic of RDS. They are composed of protein-rich fluid that lines the alveoli and impairs gas exchange.

D. Meconium-stained fluid on deep suctioning: Meconium-stained fluid is more common in term infants who are not in distress, or in infants who have been exposed to meconium in utero. It is not a typical finding in premature infants with RDS.

Final answer: C
